<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# Hypothesis: H1 | Level 2 has a large 26-block ring (outer frame) controlled by top R/N, plus independent middle/bottom rings controlled by their own R/N buttons. Goal is to align Y blocks with Y markers at (26,35) and (35,35).

# Let me click the MIDDLE red shape to see what it controls
# Middle R is at approximately (26, 14) based on the image
# Let me find its exact position from segmentation

seg = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
red_blocks = [n for n in seg if n['color'] == 'R']
for n in red_blocks:
    b = n['boundary']
    rows = [p[0] for p in b]
    cols = [p[1] for p in b]
    print(f"Red block at ({min(rows)}, {min(cols)}), pixels={n['pixels']}, boundary={b}")

# Save current state
import copy
before_state = {}
for n in seg:
    if n['pixels'] == 4 and n['color'] not in ('c', 'G', 'B'):
        b = n['boundary']
        r, c = min([p[0] for p in b]), min([p[1] for p in b])
        before_state[(r,c)] = n['color']

# Click middle red shape
action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 26, 'col': 14}])

# Check what changed
after_seg = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
after_state = {}
for n in after_seg:
    if n['pixels'] == 4 and n['color'] not in ('c', 'G', 'B'):
        b = n['boundary']
        r, c = min([p[0] for p in b]), min([p[1] for p in b])
        after_state[(r,c)] = n['color']

print("\nChanged blocks:")
for key in sorted(set(list(before_state.keys()) + list(after_state.keys()))):
    b = before_state.get(key, '?')
    a = after_state.get(key, '?')
    if b != a:
        print(f"  {key}: {b} -> {a}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

# Hypothesis: H1 | Level 2 has a large 26-block ring (outer frame) controlled by top R/N, plus independent middle/bottom rings controlled by their own R/N buttons. Goal is to align Y blocks with Y markers at (26,35) and (35,35).

    b = n['boundary']
    rows = [p[0] for p in b]
    cols = [p[1] for p in b]
    print(f"Red block at ({min(rows)}, {min(cols)}), pixels={n['pixels']}, boundary={b}")

import copy
before_state = {}

        b = n['boundary']
        r, c = min([p[0] for p in b]), min([p[1] for p in b])
        before_state[(r,c)] = n['color']

# Click middle red shape
action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 26, 'col': 14}])

# Check what changed
after_seg = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
after_state = {}
for n in after_seg:

        after_state[(r,c)] = n['color']

for key in sorted(set(list(before_state.keys()) + list(after_state.keys()))):
